title: Token monitoring & lightweight skills
intro: Context is rent. We measure token pressure and keep the harness thin: on-demand skills, requestable rules, lean tool sessions, and ruthless always-on budgets.
why: Every always-on rule, MCP catalog entry, and fat skill description is paid on every turn. Optimising tokens is not stinginess — it is how the working relationship stays fast and affordable.

practices.title: Thin skill dispatchers
practices.body: SKILL.md stays short; deep detail lives in reference.md loaded only when needed.

practices.title: Requestable by default
practices.body: Most rules are pull-when-relevant. Always-on is reserved for true P0 fail-closed constraints.

practices.title: Lean MCP sessions
practices.body: Tiny always-on core (memory + decisions + app control). Enable specialty servers for the task, then unload.

practices.title: Measure the tax
practices.body: Pulse token/structure reports when the session feels heavy. Treat catalog bloat and mega-chats as bugs.

practices.title: Encode the second burn
practices.body: If a failure repeats, write a thin skill — do not keep re-explaining in a growing chat.

practices.title: Split lanes, not prompts
practices.body: Parallel agents with clear owns beat one mega-context trying to do everything.

antiPatterns: Always-on essays that restate the whole philosophy every turn
Leaving optional MCPs loaded “just in case”
Past chats as the only memory (prompt archaeology)
Counting LOC or tokens-spent as success
